source_bindings.text: **2.** 什么是球面镜的主焦点？

Q1_expected: Incident ray, reflected ray and local normal at the point of incidence are coplanar.
Reflection angle equals incidence angle, both measured from that local normal, not the tangent surface.
For nonnormal incidence the paths are on opposite sides of the normal; at normal incidence both angles are zero and the ray returns on its own path. Opposite-sides wording must not be unconditional.
At a spherical surface the radius through curvature center O is the local normal. Principal axis is the normal only at the pole, not all points.
Local reflection law is not a paraxial-only law. A new numeric scenario can apply it but is not original-source given data.
Q2_expected: Principal-focus definition uses incident rays parallel to the principal axis, not an arbitrary oblique parallel beam.
In the paraxial small-height/small-angle model, actual reflected rays converge at the real concave focus in front of the mirror.
Convex reflected rays diverge; only their backward extensions approximately meet at the virtual focus behind the mirror.
Do not describe actual reflected rays as entering the convex mirror's rear focus.

Approximate common focusing is not exact arbitrary-wide-beam focusing. Both concave and convex definitions are source-supported in d440; independent real/virtual and paraxial explanations must not become captured bookRaw.
